definitions.explanation: Hair braided and hanging down, typically in two braids on each side of the head. Most commonly associated with girls' hairstyles.

examples.japanese: おさげの{女|おんな}の{子|こ}。

examples.english: To wear one's hair in braids.

examples.japanese: {小学生|しょうがくせい}のころ、{毎朝|まいあさ}{母|はは}におさげを{編|あ}んでもらっていた。
examples.english: When I was in elementary school, my mother braided my hair every morning.

notes:
From お{下|さ}げ, literally "hanging down" with the honorific prefix お. Originally referred to any hair hanging down the back, but now specifically means braided pigtails.

USAGE:
Strongly associated with young girls, especially schoolgirls. The image of おさげ evokes childhood and innocence in Japanese culture. Also called {三|み}つ{編|あ}み (three-strand braid) when referring to the braiding technique itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おさげの{女|おんな}の{子|こ} — a girl with braids
- おさげにする — to wear in braids
- おさげを{編|あ}む — to braid pigtails
- おさげ{髪|がみ} — braided hair

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {三|み}つ{編|あ}み — braid, plait; refers to the braiding technique
- ツインテール — twin tails; ponytails on each side (not braided)
- ポニーテール — ponytail; a single tail at the back
